content.text:
## explore (ok; 7 turns, 31k in / 1k out, 7 tool calls)

## Direct answer

**(1) Env var:** `PI_MODEL_ID` — it pins the model id registered into pi's `models.json`.
**(2) Documented value:** `.env.example` sets it to `PI_MODEL_ID=agnes-3.0-flash` (line 45); in code the fallback when unset is `agnes-3.0-flash` (term.ts/presets.ts/llm.ts) or `kimi-k2.5` (runner.ts legacy fallback).
**(3) Consuming evidence:**

- `pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src/runner.ts:41` — `export const MODEL_ID = process.env.PI_MODEL_ID || "kimi-k2.5";` This constant is the `id` written into the engine's sandboxed `models.json` in `ensureAgentDir()` at `runner.ts:223` (`{ id: MODEL_ID, ... }` under `modelsPath = join(AGENT_DIR, "models.json")`, `runner.ts:267-268`). The file-level comment at `runner.ts:194-198` states the registry exists so `PI_MODEL_ID=provider/model` routes sandboxed runs.
- `pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src/term.ts:151` — `const modelId = bridgeHealthLite?.defaultModel || process.env.PI_MODEL_ID || "agnes-3.0-flash";` inside `writeModelsJson()` (which writes `~/.unown/agent/models.json`, `term.ts:146`); the model list registration follows at `term.ts:159-170`.
- `pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src/presets.ts:31` — the `bridge` preset's `defaultModel` reads `process.env.PI_MODEL_ID || "agnes-3.0-flash"`, feeding `unown setup`'s registry writes.

## Documentation evidence

- `.env.example:43-46` — "Model + provider names the engine registers with pi's models.json. Any model id works — the llm-bridge routes unknown ids onto its default." → `PI_MODEL_ID=agnes-3.0-flash`, `PI_PROVIDER=zai-bridge`.
- `pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src/cli.ts:427` — HELP text: `PI_BRIDGE_URL/PI_MODEL_ID/PI_PROVIDER   LLM endpoint for ~/.unown/agent/models.json`.

## Details — all consumers under `pi-repo/packages/self-learning/src/`

| File:line | Role |
|---|---|
| `term.ts:151` | Terminal agent's `models.json` seed: bridge `/health` default > `PI_MODEL_ID` > `agnes-3.0-flash` (the probe precedence was added by audit M4-a D1, `term.ts:104-112`) |
| `runner.ts:41`, `:223` | Engine's sandboxed agent dir `models.json` seed: `MODEL_ID` = `PI_MODEL_ID` (or `kimi-k2.5` legacy fallback) |
| `presets.ts:31` | `unown setup` bridge-preset defaultModel |
| `llm.ts:11` | `LLM_MODEL = process.env.PI_MODEL_ID \|\| "agnes-3.0-flash"` for the engine's own LLM calls |
| `cli.ts:904-907` | `--model` flag propagates into `process.env.PI_MODEL_ID` because `term.ts:writeModelsJson` reads it at call time |
| `cli.ts:1271-1273` | per-session subagent routing writes `PI_MODEL_ID` (never clobbers models.json, which `setup` owns) |
| `termhooks.ts:517` | hook default model: `PI_MODEL_ID \|\| "agnes-3.0-flash"` |
| `subagent-routing.ts:357` | documentary: unset subagent → child uses whatever `PI_MODEL_ID` / models.json resolves to |
| `automations.ts:1156` | automation-scoped `PI_MODEL_ID` override on spawned runs |

One nuance worth noting: `term.ts:151` prefers the bridge's live `/health` `defaultModel` over `PI_MODEL_ID` on a first-run seed (fresh install only — `writeModelsJson` never clobbers an existing `models.json`, `term.ts:152`); so `PI_MODEL_ID` is the pinning variable, but on the very first seed a reachable bridge can override it with its own route default.

content.text:
## Report

| | Answer |
|---|---|
| **My finding** | `PI_MODEL_ID` — documented in `.env.example:43-45` ("Model + provider names the engine registers with pi's models.json") as `PI_MODEL_ID=agnes-3.0-flash`; consumed by `src/term.ts:151` in `writeModelsJson` (`bridgeHealthLite?.defaultModel \|\| PI_MODEL_ID \|\| "agnes-3.0-flash"`) |
| **Subagent finding** | `PI_MODEL_ID` — same `.env.example` doc block, same `term.ts:151` consumer, plus `runner.ts:41/223` (the sandboxed engine agent dir's models.json), `presets.ts:31`, `llm.ts:11`, `cli.ts:427` |
| **Agree?** | **Yes, fully.** Same variable, same doc location. |

One nuance the fresh check surfaced that I hadn't called out: `term.ts` seeds the registry with a precedence chain where a reachable bridge's live `/health` `defaultModel` beats `PI_MODEL_ID` on the first-run seed — so `PI_MODEL_ID` is the pinning env var, but a fresh install with a live bridge can be nudged to the bridge's own default. Also noted: `runner.ts` uses a legacy `kimi-k2.5` fallback for the sandboxed agent dir, vs `agnes-3.0-flash` everywhere else.
